found_values.value: 400 ms: at most 9 frames; 3 ms: at most 8 frames. Outside the panel's start-up self-test the panel keeps one request outstanding and waits up to 1000 ms for its answer, so a stall under 1000 ms receives the frames of one request only: at most 8, a 32-register write at 4 registers a frame. During the 1200 ms start-up self-test the panel sends one probe or status request at a time and the next once the last is 50 ms old and unanswered, so 400 ms holds at most 9 (at 0, 50, ... 400 ms) and 3 ms at most 1.

found_values.value: 400 ms: at most 8,511 frames; 3 ms: at most 64 frames. The tree defines no traffic on the external port, so this is the bound of a saturated bus at the port's 1000 kbit/s nominal rate (V21) with the shortest frame: a data frame is 44 + 8N bits, so 44 bits with no data, plus an interframe space of at least 3 bits, 47 µs a frame. 400,000/47 = 8,510.6 and 3,000/47 = 63.8, each rounded up for a frame that ends inside the window. A CAN FD frame is longer, so the bound holds for FD traffic too.
found_values.source: MCP2515 data sheet DS20001801K, Figure 2-1 (data frame 44 + 8N bits, page 8) and section 2.6 (interframe space at least three recessive bits), https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MCP2515-Family-Data-Sheet-DS20001801K.pdf; nominal rate from V21 (DroneCAN specification section 8, https://dronecan.github.io/Specification/8._Hardware_design_recommendations/, read 2026-09-28T12:55:16Z)

found_values.value: nominal 1000 kbit/s; CAN FD data phase 5000 kbit/s. DroneCAN's highest recommended bit rate is 1000 kbit/s. Its CAN FD transport uses a 1 Mbit/s nominal rate with the data phase at 1, 2, 4, 5 or 8 Mbit/s depending on the hardware. 5 Mbit/s is the highest data rate that the ISO 11898-2:2016 transceivers shortlisted here are specified for in full networks (TCAN1044A-Q1: up to 5 Mbps, 8 Mbps in simpler networks).

found_values.value: 0 V: not isolated. The DroneCAN connectors carry the bus ground, and CAN Ground must be connected to Ground inside the device (D-Sub pins 3 and 6). The tree states no isolation for the port.

found_values.value: 30 V DC at least on CANH and CANL, before any round 2 connector protection. The DroneCAN D-Sub and M8 connectors carry a bus power line of 23.0 to 30.0 V, 24 V nominal, beside CAN High and CAN Low. A CAN line shorted to that line sees up to 30.0 V. The Micro connector carries 5.0 to 5.5 V. The bench's 67.2 V pack (F15) is not on the port's connector.
found_values.source: https://dronecan.github.io/Specification/8._Hardware_design_recommendations/ ('Devices that deliver power to the bus are required to provide 23.0-30.0 V on the bus power line'; Micro: 5.0-5.5 V)

found_values.value: 5.5 V DC at least on CANH and CANL. The link cable carries the display's 5 V supply beside CANH and CANL (F6). The tree gives that supply no tolerance, because V81 is open. 5.5 V is the upper end DroneCAN gives a 5 V bus power line that runs beside CAN High and CAN Low (Micro connector), the only published figure found for that arrangement.

found_values.value: ±8,500 ppm (±0.85 %) for each node's clock, including temperature and ageing, with the other node's clock at the opposite limit: a node-to-node variation of 1.7 %. As a cross-check, AN754's synchronisation condition 10·tbit(A) > 10·tbit(B) + tSJW(B) with the display TWAI's SJW of 4 quanta of 50 ns (Link.md:204) allows 2.0 % node to node. The IO board's side at 8 quanta and SJW 2 allows 2.5 %. The tighter figure, 1.7 %, is taken.

found_values.value: 1000 ms, about: the IO board's link controller acknowledges before the panel's first frame. The panel hands its GPIO19 and GPIO20 to CAN about a second into boot. Its first frames are the start-up self-test's status request and probes. With one supply for both boards (owner, 2026-09-24), power reaches both at once. A frame that no node acknowledges raises the panel's transmit error count by 8 each retry, and the self-test reports 'nothing is acknowledging' at 128.
